title: Choose the Tool Catalog layout
question: Three compositions inside the settled Ransom Calling Card world. All three carry the same facts: what Ritools is, the local-only claim, and Squeeze as the one Tool that exists today. Lock one; the other two close.

options.label: Proof Sheet
options.lineage: printer's proof sheet, numbered and ruled
options.thesis: Every Tool is a numbered proof on one shared rule grid, and the local-only claim prints as the sheet's stamp.
options.viewport: A ruled sheet: the page title and the claim stamp share the first course. Below, Squeeze prints as proof 01 in a wide cell, with its promise, its real input and output facts, and an OPEN SQUEEZE mark. The sheet closes on a stamped band that carries the four promises.
options.risk: A proof grid with one filled cell can read as an unfinished catalog unless the stamped band earns the empty space.

options.label: Wanted Notice
options.lineage: pinned wanted broadside with a seal
options.thesis: Each Tool is a wanted notice: one broadside, its name cut from letters, and a LOCAL ONLY seal stamped over the sheet.
options.viewport: One tilted broadside pinned to a full-bleed paper field. The ransom SQUEEZE sits at poster scale and crops at the sheet edge; its promise, its input and output facts, and a red OPEN SQUEEZE mark follow. A round LOCAL ONLY seal stamps the lower corner, and the four promises print on the field under it.
options.risk: The broadside is a costume risk: it can read as a novelty poster and slow the route into the Tool.

options.label: Tool Shelf
options.lineage: a shop shelf under a painted claim
options.thesis: The claim owns the whole viewport at poster scale; the Tools sit on one printed shelf below it, each with a zero price tag.
options.viewport: A full-width claim in ransom and poster type fills the first viewport, with the page title and the Tool count in the top corner. One shelf crosses the bottom: Squeeze as a wide white entry with its promise and OPEN mark, beside one ruled bay that carries 'More Tools are on the way.' A red foot closes the shelf.
options.risk: The claim outranks the Tools, so a visitor hunting a specific Tool must read past the poster to find it.
